title: Steam Weekend vs Weekday Gaming Split
dataSources: Tautulli/Plex playback (`tautulli:play`), Jellyfin activity (`jellyfin:activity`), Spotify recently-played (`spotify:play`), Steam player and achievements (`steam:player`), Sonarr events (`sonarr:event`).
app: Plex / Jellyfin (Tautulli), Sonos, Spotify, Steam, Xbox/PSN, and the *arr stack (Sonarr/Radarr) APIs and webhooks via HEC scripted inputs.

description: Separates your game time into weekday and weekend buckets, revealing which titles are light decompression and which ones swallow whole Saturdays.
value: Time allocation is easier to improve when you know what owns your weekends versus your evenings; this is backlog management through telemetry.
implementation: Forward per-session or per-day Steam play minutes; refresh weekly and compare your actual game mix across the two day types.
visualization: Stacked bar chart of minutes played by game for weekdays versus weekends.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Personal HEC index — HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.
• **Subcategory context**: Media, Gaming & Entertainment — typical feeds: Tautulli/Plex playback (`tautulli:play`), Jellyfin activity (`jellyfin:activity`), Spotify recently-played (`spotify:play`), Steam player/achievements (`steam:player`), Sonarr/Radarr events (`sonarr:e.
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `steam:player`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Personal HEC index** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=steam:player`.

**Collection method:** HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `POST https://<splunk>:8088/services/collector/event`.

**Suggested poll interval:** depends on upstream connector.

**Key fields to extract:** `sourcetype-specific — see search filters`.

**Typical connector stack:** Plex / Jellyfin (Tautulli), Sonos, Spotify, Steam, Xbox/PSN, and *arr stack (Sonarr/Radarr) APIs and webhooks via HEC..

**Author notes:** Forward per-session or per-day Steam play minutes; refresh weekly and compare your actual game mix across the two day types.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "steam:player", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=steam:player earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **Steam Weekend vs Weekday Gaming Split** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=steam:player`) across the full search range. It applies numeric thresholds on `weekday` (> 5) after sum — tune these constants to your household baseline.

**Fields this search depends on:** `bucket`, `game_name`, `weekday`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=steam:player
| eval weekday=strftime(_time,"%u")
| eval bucket=if(weekday>5,"weekend","weekday")
| stats sum(minutes_played) as minutes by bucket game_name
| sort - minutes
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Splunk Search → index=personal | stats count by sourcetype. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=steam:player earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table bucket, game_name, weekday
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=steam:player earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

**(d) Threshold calibration:** Profile `weekday` before alerting:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=steam:player earliest=-30d
| stats perc50(weekday) AS p50 perc90(weekday) AS p90 perc99(weekday) AS p99 max(weekday) AS hi
```

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.7.13: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Stacked Bar Chart Of Minutes Played By Game For Weekdays Versus Weekends (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Personal HEC index — no Personal HEC index events / missing fields:** If `steam:player` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Personal HEC index connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Personal HEC index — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Personal HEC index JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=steam:player | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Personal HEC index — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Personal HEC index — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Personal HEC index APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `aggregation` buckets.
